ratings_why.fun: Every tier does its job and the Burrow gives a real spend-or-keep choice each turn, with three late builds that pull on one pile; Kit size growing only through Tunic Weaver makes the midgame Kits feel flat.
ratings_why.distinct: An off-board reserve that is fight HP, currency and ammunition at once plays unlike any of today's tribes, though at heart it is still a token-swarm tribe.

verdict_why: The tier shape is right, but 'your front unit' needs a definition and Kit size needs a second way to grow before the design settles.

points.text: Brother Onward and The Front Lemming say 'your front unit' without defining it: slot F1, or the first living front-row unit in reading order? The Banner's path depends on it.

Kit size grows only through Tunic Weaver's When played (plus Harvest Supper), so the size half of 'count times size' stalls after Tier 2. A Tier 3 or 4 card that raises Kit size each turn would give the midgame a growth curve to chase.

With Herald and Litter Keeper making about 10 Kits a turn, Ferrywife settles near a Burrow of 20 and spends 10 a turn, so every real unit gains +10/+10 a turn. That's a great capstone to chase; the owner may want to know the steady-state number.
Herding Council's +1/+1 for 2 Kits is far below Raft-builder's +2/+2 per Kit a tier lower. Letting it scale with Burrow size, or making it cheaper, would put it in the Crossing build.

Identical Cousin is the most interesting splash card, but golden Cousin turns one key unit into an instant triple. Consider limiting the golden to one copy so it stays a strong roll rather than a sure triple.

standouts.why: The Front Lemming is a clean Tier 3 card that names the comp and turns the Burrow into fight HP straight away.
Cantor of the Edge turns a long Kit chain into one giant body, a big fight-only payoff that suits the tide fantasy.
Ferrywife of the Wide Water makes the Tide-or-Crossing choice concrete every turn and gives the late game its big permanent numbers.

weakest.why: Herding Council is a low rate at Tier 4 and has a trigger condition that Ferrywife does better.
Tally is trivial inside the tribe (Kits fill the board for free) and generic outside it, so it asks no decision.
Ole the Learned does 1 to 3 damage per Kit at a typical Kit size, which is small for using up three Burrow Kits.

flags.note: Ferrywife with Herald and Litter Keeper reaches about +10/+10 a turn on every real unit, and a golden doubles that.
A Burrow of 20 or more with Old Mother Lemen and Snow Hall Guard feeds the biggest unit 100+ stats in one fight; the golden doubles it.
Golden Identical Cousin makes two copies of any adjacent unit, which is an instant triple and Discover, and can copy capstones like Brother Onward.
Old Mother Lemen plus Gerd's Bristle Kits against low-Attack boards could produce long fights and many ties.
'Your front unit' is not defined (slot F1, or first living front-row unit), and the same goes for The Front Lemming.
